s.t:
Deine Rolle
Als Product Manager BESS & PCS (m/w/d) übernimmst du die End-to-End-Verantwortung für die Produktfamilie der Outdoor-Energiespeichersysteme von STABL sowie für unsere proprietäre Leistungselektronik. Deine Mission ist es, wettbewerbsfähige, hochwertige Produkte zu gestalten, die echte Kundenbedürfnisse lösen und das Wachstum von STABL unterstützen.

Du wandelst Erkenntnisse aus Markt, Kunden und Stakeholdern in eine klare Produktausrichtung um und arbeitest funktionsübergreifend daran, das Portfolio kontinuierlich weiterzuentwickeln. Als Teil des Business Innovation Teams stellst du sicher, dass Marktfeedback klar in unsere Organisation eingebracht und anschließend umgesetzt wird.
Deine Mission
Du verwaltest nicht nur eine Roadmap – du gestaltest aktiv die nächste Generation von Energiespeichersystemen in einem hochdynamischen Umfeld. Diese Position ist ideal für jemanden, der groß denkt, gerne Hardware und Software miteinander verbindet und Produkte entwickeln möchte, die Kunden begeistern – für ein skalierendes und sich gleichzeitig kontinuierlich weiterentwickelndes Produkt in einer der am schnellsten wachsenden Branchen der Energiewende.
Du sammelst Kunden- und Marktanforderungen und übersetzt diese in klare Produktanforderungen und Prioritäten.
Du stellst die technische Exzellenz, die kommerzielle Wettbewerbsfähigkeit und die Gesamtqualität der Lösungen sicher.
Du agierst als zentrale Schnittstelle zwischen Kunden, dem Markt sowie internen und externen Stakeholdern.
Du führst Wettbewerbsanalysen und Marktforschung durch, um Trends, Chancen und Risiken zu identifizieren. Dabei arbeitest du an Systemen, die an gewerblichen und industriellen Standorten eingesetzt werden, und sorgst für die richtige Balance zwischen Leistung, Kosten und Sicherheit in einem sich schnell weiterentwickelnden regulatorischen Umfeld.
Du bereitest strategische Entscheidungsgrundlagen vor und präsentierst diese. Außerdem steuerst du Produkte und zugehörige Initiativen über den gesamten Produktlebenszyklus – von der Konzeption und Validierung bis hin zur Markteinführung und kontinuierlichen Weiterentwicklung.
Dein Profil
Mehr als 5 Jahre Erfahrung im Produktmanagement oder Product Ownership, idealerweise im Cleantech-, EPC-, Industrie-, Elektronikbereich oder einem vergleichbaren B2B-Umfeld sowie mehr als 3 Jahre Erfahrung im Bereich Energiespeicherung, idealerweise mit BESS.
Ausgeprägte Fähigkeit, Kunden-, Markt- und Geschäftsanforderungen in klare Produktanforderungen, Prioritäten und Roadmap-Entscheidungen zu übersetzen.
Nachweisbare Erfahrung im Management von Produkt-Roadmaps sowie in der bereichsübergreifenden Abstimmung mit unterschiedlichen Stakeholdern und Fachbereichen.
Starkes analytisches und strategisches Denkvermögen sowie Erfahrung in den Bereichen Marktforschung, Wettbewerbsanalyse und Produktpositionierung.
Hervorragende Kommunikations- und Stakeholder-Management-Fähigkeiten sowie die Fähigkeit, vertrauensvoll mit Kunden, Partnern und internen Teams zusammenzuarbeiten. Fließende Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse.
Strukturierte, proaktive und eigenverantwortliche Arbeitsweise; Erfahrung mit B2B-Kunden aus dem Energie- oder Infrastrukturbereich ist von Vorteil.
Warum STABL Energy?
STABL Energy gehört zu den innovativsten Start-ups der Energiewende, ist Gewinner des ees Award 2022 , des pv magazine Award 2025 und wurde als eines der Top 100 Energy Start-ups weltweit ausgezeichnet. Wir werden von renommierten und erfahrenen Tech-VCs aus Deutschland, Dänemark und der Schweiz unterstützt.
Darauf kannst du dich freuen
Agile, offene und innovationsgetriebene Unternehmenskultur mit flachen Hierarchien, schnellen Entscheidungswegen und echter Eigenverantwortung.
Betriebliche Altersvorsorge zur Unterstützung deiner Zukunftsplanung.
Flexible Arbeitszeiten, ein hybrides Arbeitsmodell sowie die Möglichkeit, zeitweise aus dem Ausland zu arbeiten.
Digitale Essensgutscheine mit Circula Lunch – genieße dein Mittagessen auf uns!
Monatlicher Sachbezug, den du bei deinen Lieblingsgeschäften einlösen kannst.

Regelmäßige Teambuilding-Aktivitäten und Team-Events.
EGYM Wellpass – trainiere ohne Limits in zahlreichen Fitnessstudios in ganz Deutschland.
Bereit, Innovation voranzutreiben, etwas zu bewegen und andere zu inspirieren? Bewirb dich jetzt!
Wir freuen uns darauf, von dir zu hören und gemeinsam mit dir das Energiesystem der Zukunft zu gestalten! Auch wenn du nicht alle Anforderungen zu 100 % erfüllst, möchten wir dich ausdrücklich ermutigen, dich zu bewerben. Unser Motto lautet „Hire for attitude, train for skills“ – deshalb schätzen wir Potenzial und lebenslanges Lernen genauso sehr wie Erfahrung.

Better Money Strike is the Bitcoin company. With Strike , you can buy and sell bitcoin, pay bills, and borrow against your holdings. From individuals to businesses, Strike is purpose-built for every step of the Bitcoin journey.

Available in more than 100 countries — including the U.S., Europe, Latin America, and Africa — Strike is building a better financial system powered by Bitcoin. Bitcoin is better money. Strike is how you use it. Role: Strike is where people around the world send, save, and spend money on bitcoin rails.

For a product like that, customer trust is a feature in and of itself.

As Trust Product Manager, you'll own the features that make customers confident keeping their money with Strike : account security controls, verified support experiences, beneficiary planning, account management, and the systems like KYC/B, transaction limits, account restrictions that keep fraudsters out without getting in the way of good customers.

You'll ship customer-facing features, and you'll own the foundations underneath them, turning what most companies treat as friction into experiences customers actually appreciate.

You'll succeed by shipping trust-building features customers love, minimizing fraud, maintaining compliance, and protecting the health and integrity of the Strike ecosystem. This position is available for candidates located in the eastern US time zone.

What You’ll Do: Serve as the voice of the customer (internal customer too!) and intimately understand the products we offer as well as their potential fraud vectors and blind spots Work closely with Compliance, Finance, Operations, and Data to uncover and understand needs Partner with cross-functional peers to define, prioritize, and deliver a roadmap and product that maximize impact to financial risk management and our fraud strategy Own our Fraud KPIs and partner with Data and Finance to iterate on their definition as needed Establish and track success metrics for various features and initiatives, including operational efficiencies Support and motivate cross-functional teams through an inclusive and collaborative mindset Qualifications: At least 4 years of experience in product management, with at least 2 of those years in trust/fraud related teams A highly experimental mindset to drive innovation amidst uncertainty or ambiguity (e.g., new processes, teams, systems) Vast experience working with designers and user researchers Empathy to work with a diverse array of cross functional peers and stakeholders Resourcefulness, pragmatism and roll-up the sleeves mentality Excellent verbal and written communication skills Experience and interest for Bitcoin and Fintech is a plus US-Based Positions Salary range: $162K - 190K Equity in a high-growth startup Health, dental, and vision insurance premium contributions; short & long-term disability insurance and basic life insurance Cell phone and internet reimbursement Flexible PTO, sick leave & parental leave Access to a company 401k plan We do not make hiring decisions based on educational history whatsoever.

Our Founder is a college dropout. We employ high school dropouts, PHD candidates and everything in-between. We do not hire credentials. We simply hire talented, passionate individuals who are excited to be a part of our team.

We’re hiring a Staff Product Manager to help shape the future of our products and drive company-wide impact! This is a senior-level, subject-matter-expert role that combines strategic vision with hands-on leadership across multiple teams.

The Product team works to design, develop, and manage user-centered digital products that align with our business goals. Through close collaboration with stakeholders, user feedback, and data-driven insights, we deliver innovative and reliable solutions that move the business forward.

Reporting to the Director of Product, you’ll define and deliver a 2–3 year product strategy that aligns with the company’s long-term vision. You’ll work closely with Product and Engineering leadership to shape development practices, influence roadmaps, and ensure consistent product direction across teams.

As an individual contributor and domain expert, you’ll raise the bar for Product Management through mentorship, technical depth, and scalable processes that promote fact-based problem solving and continuous improvement. This is a remote-first role within the GTA.

Responsibilities: Act as a strategic thought leader, creating clear and inspiring narratives that align teams and stakeholders around a shared product vision.

Define, own, and gain buy-in for the 2-3 year product vision of the assigned domain, and develop a concrete 18-24 month strategy and roadmap that ensures alignment with the overall product and business strategy. Collaborate with Product leaders to co-develop and optimize the overarching 18-24 month product strategy and roadmap.

Partner with Product leadership to shape cross-domain priorities, coordinate resources, and maintain alignment across multiple teams. Serve as the strategic hub and arbiter for product and development teams, resolving significant dependencies and conflicting priorities to drive successful delivery.

Lead end-to-end problem solving from strategy to execution, balancing business and technical needs to maximize impact and ROI. Proactively identify high-value opportunities, assess risks, and align stakeholders on the best path forward.

Collaborate with Engineering leadership to ensure the future state of the product and technical strategy aligns with long-term goals. Establish and share best practices that strengthen strategic planning and execution across the Product team.

Partner with Product and Engineering leaders to raise the organization’s overall strategic and delivery capabilities. Mentor Product Managers on advanced discovery, stakeholder alignment, and strategic execution.

Requirements: University degree or college diploma in a recognized technical, vocational or academic program (preferably in Engineering or Computer Science) or equivalent work 10+ years of experience in digital or software Product Management. 5+ years of experience as a senior individual contributor or an equivalent role in Product Management, with proven hands-on experience leading and implementing company-wide strategic initiatives across multiple product domains and teams.

Proven success owning the full product lifecycle, from 0 to 1 through scale, ideally in a complex, customer-facing platform or self-serve digital product. Strong ability to dive into technical architecture, understand complex data flows, and make informed decisions about platform, infrastructure, and APIs.

Skilled in building and executing product strategy and long-term roadmaps that tie to business outcomes. Deep understanding of strategic frameworks, linking day-to-day execution with long-term company value. Advanced experience in feature planning, resource management, and prioritization across multiple teams.

Proven track record of improving and scaling product processes in collaboration with product leadership. Strong discovery skills, consistently identifying the right problems, validating with data, and applying structured frameworks.

What You Bring: A thoughtful, data-driven approach to decision making and the confidence to prioritize what matters most. A genuine passion for developing the product craft and problem-solving skills of other product managers. Clear and persuasive communication skills, especially when working with executives and cross-functional teams.

You can work independently, navigate ambiguity with ease, and deliver results. Strategic thinking with a systems mindset, anticipating how today’s decisions shape tomorrow’s outcomes. A collaborative and growth-oriented mindset with a passion for mentoring and elevating other Product Managers.

s.t:
Du identifizierst Kundenbedürfnisse zielgerichtet, denkst lösungsorientiert und liebst es, technische Anforderungen auf den Punkt zu bringen? Dann werde Teil unseres agilen Teams und sorge dafür, dass aus Ideen smarte Softwarelösungen entstehen. Dabei übernimmst du folgende Aufgaben:
Du verantwortest das technische Anforderungsmanagement für ein GitOps-Tool im Behördenumfeld
Du bist die zentrale Ansprechperson für die externen und internen Kund:innen des Entwicklungsteams und übersetzt deren Anforderungen
Du formulierst und priorisierst technische Konzepte, Epics und User Stories mit dem Entwicklungsteam
Du koordinierst die operative Arbeit des Developer-Teams mit einem Scrum Master und behältst Qualität, Budget und Fortschritt im Blick
Du unterstützt die Head of Product in fachlich-strategischen Themen
Du präsentierst Produktlösungen verständlich für technische und nicht-technische Stakeholder wie z.B. Kunden
Qualifikation

Du bringst eine Ausbildung als Fachinformatiker für Systemintegration, ein Informatikstudium oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation mit, verfügst über exzellente Deutschkenntnisse (C2) und fühlst dich im direkten Kundenkontakt wohl. Diese Erfahrungen erleichtern dir den Einstieg:
Mehrjährige Erfahrung als DevOps- oder Cloud-Engineer
Erfahrung im technischen Requirements Engineering oder als (technischer) Product Owner in einem agilen Umfeld
Ein gutes technisches Verständnis von Containerisierung und Softwareentwicklung (SDLC, CI/CD, Architektur)
Erfahrung im Umgang mit Kennzahlen (z. B. DORA-Metriken, KPIs) und Projektmanagement
Kommunikationsstärke, Moderationstalent und die Fähigkeit, technische Inhalte verständlich zu vermitteln

Bei Cloudogu arbeitest du an technologisch relevanten Themen rund um Open Source, Cloud-native Technologien und digitaler Souveränität. Dabei übernimmst du früh Verantwortung und gestaltest die Zusammenarbeit zwischen Kund:innen, Produktmanagement und Entwicklung aktiv mit.
Die Rolle bietet dir die Option, dich zur/zum Product Owner weiterzuentwickeln. Gleichzeitig arbeitest du in einem Umfeld, das pragmatische Lösungen, Eigenverantwortung und moderne Zusammenarbeit fördert.
Wenn du gerne Menschen, Technik und Projekte zusammenbringst und spürbaren Impact schaffen möchtest, dann ist Cloudogu dein space to be.

Reddit is a community of communities. It’s built on shared interests, passion, and trust, and is home to the most open and authentic conversations on the internet. Every day, Reddit users submit, vote, and comment on the topics they care most about. With 100,000+ active communities and approximately 126 million daily active unique visitors, Reddit is one of the internet’s largest sources of information. For more information, visit www.redditinc.com .

The Ads Marketplace team is a strategic growth engine for Reddit Ads. Our mission is to democratize high-performance advertising by enabling brands to achieve world-class results with minimal friction. To achieve this, we need an incredibly robust, scalable, and state-of-the-art Machine Learning infrastructure.

The Ads ML Platform team is at the core of this mission, tasked with building the foundation that powers all of our content understanding, ad targeting, and ad ranking models. We are empowering our ML engineers and data scientists to move faster and build smarter.

As the Senior Product Manager for the Ads ML Platform, you will hold significant ownership over the infrastructure and tools that make our ads marketplace intelligent. You will define the vision and build the roadmap for a platform that enables unparalleled engineering velocity and supports the most modern ML architectures.
You will be the bridge between complex ML systems and business outcomes. Whether it's integrating generative AI to increase developer productivity, establishing unified model-serving infrastructure, or optimizing GPU utilization, your work will directly accelerate how quickly and effectively we can ship highly-performant ad products. If you are passionate about the intersection of platform engineering and state-of-the-art ML research, this is the role for you.

Define the Vision: Shape the long-term strategy and roadmap for Reddit’s Ads ML platform, ensuring we are adopting cutting-edge technologies (including Generative AI and LLM workflows) to stay ahead of the curve.
Accelerate Velocity: Build products and tooling that dramatically reduce friction for Machine Learning Engineers (MLEs) and Data Scientists, enabling them to train, deploy, and iterate on models faster than ever.
Cross-Functional Leadership: Partner deeply with Engineering, Data Science, and Ads Product teams to understand their constraints, prioritize platform initiatives, and deliver scalable infrastructure.
Drive Execution and Adoption: Own key performance indicators (KPIs) around platform reliability, latency, cost-efficiency, usage metrics, and developer productivity.
Stay Cutting-Edge: Keep your finger on the pulse of the broader ML ecosystem. Read the latest research papers, understand emerging architectures, and determine how they can be practically applied to Reddit’s Ads ML platform.
Distill pain points, translate to requirements : Conduct regular user research with MLEs in Ranking, Creative Effectiveness and Content Understanding to convert pain points (e.g., slow backfills, limited training speed, no way to quickly share features across models) into precise product requirements. Validate the needs and ensure they are tied into a broader vision for the org.

Experienced product manager with prior focus internal technical products, developer tools, data/ML platforms, and/or ads and content ranking.
Deeply analytical and highly technical background; you are comfortable working in complex data systems and understanding the entire machine learning lifecycle (training, inference, deployment, monitoring).
Genuine passion for machine learning and AI; you stay at the forefront of ML, enjoy reading ML research papers, stay informed on the latest industry trends, architectures, and capabilities.
Exceptional problem-solving skills and the ability to translate highly technical constraints (e.g., GPU scheduling, latency budgets) into actionable product roadmaps.
Strong communication skills; you can seamlessly translate technical requirements to business stakeholders and articulate business goals to engineering teams.

Prior professional experience as a Machine Learning Engineer, Data Scientist, or Backend Software Engineer before transitioning into Product Management.
Understanding of the Ad Tech ecosystem (bidding, ranking, targeting).
Experience implementing or managing systems that support Generative AI/LLM workflows (Agentic automation, Prompt iteration, Fine-tuning, RAG).
100% remote opportunity (we have 4 office locations for hybrid/onsite work preference in NY, SF, LA and Chicago)

Comprehensive health benefits (medical, dental, vision) & workplace perks (home office set up stipend etc)
Generous 401k matching
Flexible vacation policy

Family planning support

We build software to enable sustainable agriculture supply chains.
~31% of global GHG emissions originate from food-related activities. For the first time in history, climate performance has become an overall business performance indicator.

Enterprises are mandated by regulatory bodies to disclose their climate performance, which leads to increasing pressure from investors, competitors, retailers, and consumers to prevent and reduce their CO2e emissions. Enterprise software and new business processes can help - to make processes in the day-to-day more efficient, connect farmers better to their partners and thus, enable action in supply chains.

Today Root is the #1 primary data collection platform for dairy in DACH. We are AI-enabled at the core and driving the AI transformation across the food and agri world. The next chapter is bigger.

Build on top of Europe's #1 primary data collection platform and bring it to new heights - new markets, new commodities, ready for action. You will own our core product line end-to-end. Today it is the leading platform in Europe for collecting farm-level data at scale. Tomorrow it needs to be the foundation that powers the next decade of agricultural decarbonization. Drive expansion into new markets and commodities. Run discovery in new geographies, pressure-test our offering with local customers, decide where we double down and where we pull back.
Make it action-ready. Data collection is the foundation. Reduction is where customer value compounds. Shape how our primary data product becomes the launchpad for everything we build on top of it.

In partnership with one of the largest financial conglomerates, we are creating a secure, transparent, and high-performance trading infrastructure that can support institutional volumes while remaining accessible to retail participants.

Our strategy to achieve this is by first bringing in Japanese RWAs on-chain, and then eventually all kinds of global assets. We are building Strium , a next-generation DeFi L1 blockchain powered by a decentralized exchange with a fully on-chain order book, supporting both spot and perpetual trading, and more.

You already have strong, specific opinions about how Hyperliquid, Aster, dydx, and Drift have made their product choices. You follow the design space — funding mechanisms, oracle construction, ADL versus insurance-fund tradeoffs, cross- versus isolated-margin accounting — closely enough to argue for a position, not just summarize what others have shipped. You probably actively trade perps yourself.
We are seeking a Senior Product Manager, Trading with deep, hands-on experience shipping product at an orderbook trading venue to work on Strium – a DeFi L1 blockchain with an on-chain orderbook exchange. You will own a core surface of the exchange — order types and margin, the programmatic / API trading surface, or listings and risk parameters — and ship its v1 in partnership with engineering, risk, and our market making partners.
You will operate as the primary product interface to market makers and high-volume traders, translating their requirements into specifications that engineering can build against, and pushing back when the right answer for the venue differs from the loudest voice. You will define how we measure ourselves against similar products such as Hyperliquid, Aster, dydx, and the DEXs that matter, and run honest reviews against those benchmarks.
This role offers an opportunity to shape the product direction of our exchange at an early stage, working alongside a distributed team of engineers and traders building next-generation financial infrastructure. You will start by shipping v1 of your core surface, and over time help expand the venue's surface area into adjacent territory — lending markets, hedging and basis-trade flows, structured surfaces — as the product matures. The role reports to the Head of Product.
Why this role matters
You will own a core surface of Strium and ship its v1. The decisions you make in the first 90 days set the bar for how the venue behaves under real volume. You will be the product voice that market makers, traders, and engineers align around. If that is the work you have been looking for, this is the chair.
Team and stakeholders
Reports to the Head of Product.
Daily collaboration with engineering, risk, and our market making partners.
Frequent engagement with institutional counterparties.

Own the product strategy and v1 spec for a core trading surface — order types and margining, the programmatic / API surface, or listings and risk parameters. The specific surface will be aligned in the first week.
Act as the primary product interface to market makers and high-volume traders , turning their input into spec and maintaining a coherent product direction across competing requests.

Define which markets to list, on what timeline, and against which benchmark venues.
Set initial market parameters: leverage caps, tick / lot size, funding cap, oracle source, margin requirements.
Coordinate engineering, risk, and MM readiness for each launch.
Partner with engineering on the matching engine, risk engine, and API contracts , contributing to spec reviews and design decisions such as ADL versus insurance-fund design, cross- versus isolated-margin accounting, and oracle integration.
Define and track product success metrics — depth, slippage, fill rate, API latency, listings velocity, MM uptime etc.
Build and maintain the competitive intelligence function for the exchange: deeply understand what competitor venues have shipped, what they got right, and where the open ground is.
Write the specs, RFCs, and MM briefs that align engineering, risk, and external partners. Pre-product is a writing-heavy role.
Act as the primary product interface to institutional and incumbent-finance counterparties, translating their requirements into specifications and maintaining a coherent venue direction across these stakeholders.
Beyond v1 of your initial surface, contribute to the design of adjacent surfaces — lending markets, hedging and basis-trade flows, structured surfaces — and seed the groundwork during early shipping so future expansion is not a rewrite.

Exchange Product Experience
5–8 years of product management experience, with 2+ years shipping product at an orderbook trading venue (derivatives, CEX or DEX).
You worked on the trading or exchange team .
You have owned a roadmap with market makers and institutional traders as a real stakeholder .
Trading Literacy
Fluent in trader vocabulary: funding, basis, skew, taker / maker, ADL, oracle slippage, latency-sensitive flow.
Familiarity with the operational mechanics of perp markets — liquidation engines, insurance funds, cross- and isolated-margin, funding rate design, mark price construction.
Strong, specific opinions about other DEXs' product choices: what they got right, what's still open, and what you would do differently.
You actively trade perps with non-trivial volume.

Track record of shipping in pre-PMF environments. You can define your own surface and scope rather than executing against an inherited roadmap.
Comfortable making decisions without a research team behind you.
Communication & Writing

Ability to communicate clearly with both engineers and external trading partners, in their own register.
Japanese language proficiency is preferred but not required, given regular engagement with Japanese partners and counterparties.
Technical Fluency
Technical enough that engineers respect you in design review.
Comfortable reading code and understanding what's happening under the hood.
Strong Plus
New Venue Launch
You have launched a new orderbook trading venue from zero.
Quant or Trading Background
You have done quant, market-making, or trading work yourself, in a professional or serious personal capacity.
Onchain Risk Infrastructure
Experience with oracle design, liquidation auctions, or cross-margin accounting on-chain.
Asia Market Context
Familiarity with Japanese or APAC capital markets, retail trading culture, or institutional trading workflows.
Lending Protocols
Familiarity with the design space of on-chain lending and money markets (Aave, Morpho, Drift's lending surface, etc.) and how they interact with leveraged trading.
Hedging & Structured Products
Experience with hedging desks, basis-trade flows, or structured products from traditional finance or crypto.
Incumbent Finance Product Experience
You have shipped product inside or alongside an incumbent financial institution — a broker-dealer, prime broker, established exchange, or asset manager — and understand how they evaluate, integrate, and operate trading venues.

s.h: Your Mission This is a company built for growth, not comfort.
s.t:
When you join exmox, you're stepping onto a global, highly competitive playing field, solving real problems in environments that push you beyond your comfort zone.
We build high-performing consumer products in one of the most competitive industries there is: mobile gaming, leading one of its largest innovations, a rewarded user engagement and acquisition platform that helps publishers acquire and retain players through rewarding experiences.
Senior Product Manager (f/m/x) isn't just about shipping features, it's about building products that perform.

Product at exmox means understanding the bigger business picture, considering cross-functional impact across Engineering, Data, Marketing, and Operations, and turning strategy into product decisions that create real value, knowing every change you ship affects millions of users.

At exmox, we're also embracing AI as part of how we work, not just what we build. We use AI tools to work smarter, cut down on repetitive tasks and spend our time where it actually moves the needle. If that mindset speaks to you, you'll fit right in.
If you're energized by dynamic markets, complex products, and the challenge of building products that perform at scale, we want to hear from you.
What You’ll Own: Own one of exmox's highest-impact product domains end-to-end, shaping the reward economy through payout thresholds, tiering, bonuses, promotions, and other key levers that drive profitability.
Drive activation, retention, and long-term engagement through onboarding experiences, streaks, quests, progression systems, reactivation flows, and other lifecycle initiatives.
Take new growth opportunities from first hypothesis to go/no-go decision, across product, market expansion, partnerships, and distribution.
Lead a high-quality experimentation process by defining hypotheses, designing statistically sound A/B tests, interpreting results, and making data-driven product decisions.
Partner closely with your dedicated Data Analyst to uncover opportunities, validate assumptions, and continuously improve product performance.
Work with Engineering, Design, Commercial, User Acquisition, Customer Support, Fraud, and Leadership to align priorities and deliver impactful product improvements.
Represent your product domain directly to leadership, using data, customer insights, and business context to influence strategic decisions.
What Success Looks Like: You take ownership quickly: Within your first months, you've become the trusted owner of a critical product domain, confidently driving priorities, making decisions, and reducing dependency on leadership.
Growth metrics measurably improve: Your product strategy and experimentation drive meaningful improvements in activation, retention, and long-term user profitability.
Product decisions are driven by data: Experiments, user insights, and product analytics provide clear evidence to prioritize opportunities, validate ideas, and confidently decide what to scale - or stop.
Cross-functional teams are aligned around outcomes: You partner closely with Engineering, Design, Data, Commercial, and User Acquisition to deliver product improvements that balance user value with business impact.
You turn ambitious ideas into scalable growth: Through structured experimentation, clear prioritization, and continuous optimization, you build product experiences that become repeatable growth levers for the business.
You outgrow the role: We are hiring for the ceiling, not just the opening. This role is scoped to grow - mentoring other product managers first, and leading a product team as we scale, if that is the direction you want to take.
What You Bring Experienced: You bring 5+ years of Product Management experience in consumer-facing digital products, ideally within mobile apps, gaming, marketplaces, subscriptions, ad-tech, fintech, or other high-growth B2C businesses. You have owned consumer product at scale - hundreds of thousands of monthly active users or more.
Business-Oriented: You understand that product decisions are business decisions. You're comfortable balancing user needs, commercial objectives, and technical constraints to maximize long-term value.
Fluent in Incentives: You have a real feel for why people come back and what makes a reward feel worth the effort. You have designed incentive, reward or progression mechanics and calibrated them so they motivate without eroding margin.
Experimentation-Driven: You have extensive experience running A/B tests, defining hypotheses, interpreting data, and making evidence-based product decisions. Statistical thinking comes naturally to you.
Data-Literate: You're comfortable working with product metrics and collaborating closely with analysts to uncover insights, measure success, and prioritize opportunities.
Strategic & Hands-on: You enjoy defining product strategy while remaining deeply involved in execution - from writing specifications and refining solutions to reviewing experiment results and driving delivery.
Collaborative: You build strong partnerships across Product, Engineering, Design, Analytics, Marketing, Commercial, and Leadership, bringing people together around clear product goals.
Intellectually Honest: You're comfortable working in ambiguity, take ownership without waiting for direction, and thrive in fast-moving environments where priorities evolve quickly. You also kill your own ideas when the data says so - being wrong early is cheaper than being right late.
How We Win Speed is the feature. Speed beats rocket science. We move fast, test fast, and multiply our pace with AI, because action creates information and small wins compound. A fast failure is a lesson we learn from, a slow one is a problem we can't afford.
Focus on the essential. Done is better than perfect. We stay focused on what actually moves us forward and protect people's time from anything that doesn't. We're direct in how we communicate too, no rambling, no unnecessary detail.
See it. Own it. Solve it. The first to see it is best placed to fix it. We're not a place for comfort, we're a place for doers. "Not my job" isn't in our vocabulary, if you spot something, you help make sure it gets solved.

Airtm’s solution is a swift and comprehensive financial platform that facilitates low-value cross-border payments and local cash-outs. As pioneers in stablecoin-payment infrastructure, Airtm has built the most advanced cross-border payment system available on the market.
As a company married to the world of online work, Airtm will go beyond payments to build the necessary infrastructure the online-work economy needs to thrive. Hypofriend is a next-generation online mortgage advisor using proprietary technology to find customers the best mortgage possible and give holistic financial advice.
Unlike other mortgage advisors or brokers, we use financial insights to guide our customers. By joining us, you will be able to tap into these insights and be part of our path to transform the industry. We provide customers with tools that help them navigate the entire home buying process, from making buying decisions and give advice on the next steps to build wealth in Germany.
As Product Manager you own a slice of that machine end-to-end: the internal platform our advisors and operations team run on, and the AI and automation that make the mortgage process faster and less manual. You will work closely with engineering, design, advisors, and the founders.
Tasks
Own your product area end-to-end — from problem discovery and prioritisation to spec, launch, and measurement.
Build for our advisors and ops team. Improve the CRM, advisory and application workflows, document handling, and lender submission so advisors spend their time advising, not administrating.
Ship AI and automation into the mortgage journey — document extraction and verification, AI-assisted advisory prep, decision support, and agentic workflows — with clear guardrails for accuracy and compliance.
Connect the dots across the funnel. Understand how the customer-facing product, advisor tooling, and lender/partner integrations affect each other, and make trade-offs across them.
Learn the business deeply enough to find the levers. Understand our advice and sales principles, how the market works, and how advisors, banks and agents actually move a case forward. Use that to spot where the business loses value — drop-offs, rework, waiting time — and where a product change unblocks it. A roadmap here is a set of bets on levers, not a wish list of features.
Define success with numbers. Set metrics per initiative (conversion, time-to-offer, advisor capacity per case, automation rate, error rate), instrument them, and report honestly on outcomes.
Write clear specs and keep delivery moving. Groom the backlog, run rituals, unblock engineers, and make the call when scope has to be cut.
Work within a regulated domain. Partner with compliance and our lending partners so what we ship holds up under German mortgage regulation.

2–4 years in product management, ideally on a product with real operational complexity (fintech, marketplace, internal tooling, or workflow automation).
Comfort with numbers and data — you can write your own SQL queries or analyses rather than waiting for someone else.
A practical grasp of what today's AI models can and cannot be trusted with, and how to design around that.
A solid UX foundation — you understand how interface and interaction design shape behaviour, and you can design flows that guide advisors and the CSM team towards the right action instead of just exposing more fields and buttons.
Strong written communication and the ability to make complex financial mechanics feel simple.
Structured, self-directed, and comfortable in a small team where you own the outcome, not just the ticket.
Fluent English. German is a strong plus (our lenders, contracts, and regulation are German).
Interest in mortgages, real estate, or personal finance — the domain rewards people who go deep.

Experience with process automation, document AI, or LLM-based product features in production.
Background in lending, insurance, or another regulated financial product.
Some technical fluency — you can read an API contract and discuss architecture trade-offs with engineers.

Big scope, real impact. Three brands and one shared financial picture — a wide surface for a team this size, and decisions that visibly move the business.
Fast pace. We ship, learn and correct quickly instead of planning quarters in advance.

Genuinely hard problems. Optimisation across lender rules, tax logic, risk and long-term financial outcomes, plus AI and automation applied to a regulated, high-stakes process.
How we work — and who thrives here

s.h: This will be a good fit if you
s.t:
Take initiative by default. When something is unclear or broken, you go and find out, rather than waiting for a decision to arrive.
Solve problems from first principles. You dig into messy, ambiguous situations, form your own view of the root cause, and propose a way forward.
Learn fast and enjoy it. Mortgages, German regulation, lender logic, our internal systems — a lot to absorb, and you will be expected to get up to speed largely on your own.
Handle context switching. On any given day you may move between an AI experiment, an advisor workflow bug, a lender requirement and a data question — and hold several threads open at once without dropping them.

Prefer one clearly scoped project at a time with minimal interruption.
Want a defined process, an existing playbook, and clear direction on what to work on next.
See the PM role mainly as writing tickets and coordinating rather than digging into the domain and the numbers yourself.
Are uncomfortable making decisions with incomplete information, or need consensus before moving.

Month 1–2: You know the mortgage process end-to-end, have shadowed advisors on real cases, and can articulate the core pillars of our workflow.
Month 3–4: You own a defined area, have a prioritised roadmap for it, and have shipped at least one improvement with a measurable effect on advisor efficiency or conversion.
Month 5–6: You are the go-to person for your domain, running discovery independently, and one AI/automation initiative is live and demonstrably reducing manual work per case.

We build technology that makes healthcare simpler, safer and more connected. Within that mission, the OMRON Connect app plays a critical role as the global front door for millions of users measuring and tracking their health. This Product Owner role ensures that foundation becomes stable, scalable and ready for the next wave of growth.
As Product Owner within the OMRON Connect team, you take ownership of a key part of a globally used consumer health app. You are responsible for turning a legacy-heavy product area into a lean, stable and cost-efficient foundation. The role sits at the intersection of product, engineering and international stakeholders, with a strong focus on prioritisation, quality and clarity. You will be making hard trade-offs daily in a high-impact, high-scale environment.
This role is central to how we improve the reliability and scalability of a product that directly influences hardware sales and long-term user engagement. Your work enables us to move faster in the future by first fixing the fundamentals. By bringing structure to complexity, you help reduce technical debt, increase delivery speed and improve product quality across the board. In short: you make it possible for the wider organisation to build with confidence.

You own a critical part of the OMRON Connect app and are responsible for making sure it delivers maximum user and business value with minimal complexity. You operate in a cross-functional, international team and act as the key decision-maker for what gets prioritised, built, improved or removed.

Drive aggressive descoping to ensure the smallest valuable increments are delivered, while actively reducing technical debt and legacy complexity.
Align a broad international stakeholder landscape and secure clear buy-in on priorities, trade-offs and scope decisions.
Translate fragmented input from stakeholders and users into clear, actionable backlog items that guide engineering effectively.
Own and communicate product vision and roadmap across strategic, tactical and operational levels.
Track and interpret key KPIs (e.g. pairing success, measurement success, data quality, adoption) to continuously refine priorities.
Long term, this role strengthens our ability to operate at global scale. By simplifying and stabilising a complex legacy landscape, you unlock capacity for innovation instead of maintenance. You also help us mature how we work with international stakeholders and regulated environments, improving decision-making speed and consistency. That combination - technical stability and organisational clarity - is what allows us to grow sustainably without increasing chaos.

The best developers don't wait for a customer to tell them something's broken.
They catch it first, in the pull request, in staging, or in the checkout flow at 3am, before a single user notices. That instinct is Checkly's whole reason to exist. We give developers and their agents the tools to own reliability the way they own their code: monitoring defined as code, powered by OpenTelemetry and Playwright, versioned and reviewed like everything else they ship. From pull request to post-mortem, in one place.
Thousands of them, from modern AI companies like Mistral and resolve.ai to large engineering orgs like LinkedIn, Citi, and 1Password, build with us. Now we need a PM who wants to take that further, in a market being rewritten in real time.
Here's the thing about 2026: AI agents and coding assistants are shipping more software, faster, than any team could review by hand, and more of it is breaking in ways nobody has seen before. LLM-backed features fail probabilistically. Agents take actions no runbook anticipated. "Is my app healthy?" is becoming an unanswerable question for a whole generation of AI-native software. Nobody has really figured out what reliability means for this kind of software yet. That's the problem you'd own.
As a Product Manager, you will be responsible for empowering developers and designers to solve customer problems. You will work directly with our SVP Product Engineering Daniel .

Shape company and product strategy alongside our SVP of Product Engineering. It's a genuine partnership: you'll develop the vision for where Checkly goes next, decide where we play in the AI testing, monitoring, and observability landscape and where we don't, and turn that into a direction. You build the strategy with us, not execute someone else's.
Shape Checkly's point of view on reliability in an AI-native world: how teams monitor AI-generated code, agent-driven workflows, and LLM-backed features
Lead initiatives across Product Engineering, Sales and Marketing, and represent Checkly directly to customers and in developer communities.
Live in the product and the problem. Empathy for DevOps, SRE and Platform Engineering isn't a line item. It's the job.
You ship with AI where it helps and know when not to. You don't just talk about it.
What you should have
You've built software before this. You're an ex-engineer, ex-founder, or ex-solutions engineer who has written real code and shipped real things, and now you want to own the product. This one's non-negotiable: you should be able to reason about APIs, MCPs, CLIs, and how systems fit together without a translator.
You've worked in a startup, not just a big company. You're comfortable with ambiguity, small teams, and owning outcomes end to end. You don't need a big-company machine around you to be effective.
You've built technical products, ideally developer tools. Adjacent technical products count. Experience in monitoring or observability is a nice-to-have, not a requirement.
New to the PM title? That's fine. If you're coming from a founding or solutions-engineering seat and want to go all-in on product, we want to hear from you.
You're technical enough to be dangerous with AI tooling. You can prototype in code, throw together a mock, or pressure-test technical viability yourself when it moves things forward.

s.h: What you will hate about us
s.t:
We would rather tell you now than have you find out in month two.
We use AI for everything, and we mean everything. AI skepticism is not a thing here. If you have the slightest hesitation about working with AI every day, this is not the place for you, and that is completely fine.
We write more than we talk. We are async-first, so a lot of decisions happen in documents and threads, not meetings. If you do your best thinking out loud in a room full of people, you will miss it here.
We are lean, so you own the boring parts too. There is no PM ops layer to delegate the unglamorous work to. You will do strategy one hour and clean up a messy spec the next.
We ship constantly and change our minds. Priorities move as we learn from customers. If you need long, stable planning cycles, this will feel chaotic.
Customer signals come first, and most of the time they beat your gut. We build what customers actually want, not the clever thing we dreamed up. Earn it by making customers happy, and then there is room for the moonshots. If you want to lead with your own bold bets, you will find this frustrating.

Flex is building the AI-native private bank for super premium, closely held business owners.
We are re-architecting the entire financial system for entrepreneurs. From the first dollar a business earns to how that value compounds, moves, and is ultimately spent in real life. Banking, credit, payments, personal finance, financial operations, all rebuilt from the ground up as a single intelligent system.
Since launching publicly in September 2023, we have scaled from zero to nine-figure annualized revenue with a clear path to profitability by late 2026. We move fast, ship relentlessly, and operate with extreme ownership.
Our customers are affluent business owners with $3M to $200M in revenue. The backbone of the economy and one of the most underserved segments in finance. We are replacing the outdated banks and fragmented tools they are stuck with. The opportunity is a roughly $1T+ revenue market hiding in plain sight. We are building toward $100B+ in enterprise value by delivering a product that is fundamentally better, not incrementally improved.
Flex has raised $100M+ in equity and $300M+ in debt.
What we hold ourselves to: mission-critical problems, high bar low ego, speed over comfort, enduring impact.
Locations: Remote. Open to candidates in Canada, Mexico, the United States, Brazil, and Colombia.

--------
You will own Flex's Accountants Stack. Accounting integrations, expense management, bill pay, invoicing, AR and AP, and financial reporting. The full set of tools that closely held business owners and the accountants who serve them use to run the financial operations of the company.
The accountant is the lead persona for this role. Bookkeepers, controllers, fractional CFOs, and outside CPAs are the people who actually live in this software day to day. Build for them and the owner wins by default. Build only for the owner and the accountant works around you, which means you lose.
The reason this role exists at Flex and not at every fintech is the unique customer we serve.

Super premium business owners with $3M to $200M in revenue have a controller or an outside accountant, real ERP systems (NetSuite, Sage Intacct, sometimes Microsoft Dynamics or Acumatica), and a layered financial life where the business and personal sides are deeply intertwined.

The owner pays themselves a distribution, then funds personal investments, then pays for an asset, then expenses something back through the company. Their accountant has to make all of it tie out. We are the only product positioned to make that integrated life elegant for both sides. This role builds it.
You will not build a generic accounting integration. You will build the Accountants Stack that bookkeepers, controllers, and CPAs actually want, which means knowing what they hate about QuickBooks, what they love about NetSuite, what they wish Bill.com did, and where the seams between business and personal finance create the most friction today.

----------------
Define the strategy and own the connectivity layer to the accounting and ERP systems our customers' accountants use. QuickBooks Online, Xero, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, etc.
Build expense management that works for owners and the accountants reconciling on their behalf. Receipt capture, GL coding, approval workflows, integration into the accounting tools without requiring manual reconciliation downstream.
Own bill pay and AR/AP. The workflow from invoice received to vendor paid, from invoice sent to customer paid, with full reconciliation back to the accounting system.
Build the invoicing product. We do not have a real invoicing offering today and customers are starting to ask. Decide what shape it takes and ship it.
Architect the connection between business financial data and personal financial data. This is the wedge no other fintech has. Make the integrated owner life real in product so the accountant can deliver it cleanly.
Partner closely with the Banking, Credit, Cards, and Payments product owners so financial flows tie out cleanly across the stack. No seams. No reconciliation tax for the accountant or the customer.
Translate the controller, CFO, and CPA persona for the rest of the company. We need someone who speaks both owner and accountant fluently. And can translate it to the owner mindset.
What you will need
------------------
You have spent years thinking about how business owners and the accountants who serve them actually run financial operations. You know the difference between a bookkeeper, a controller, a fractional CFO, and an outside accountant, and you have built product for at least one of them.
Deep, hands-on familiarity with at least two of: QuickBooks Online, Xero, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, Acumatica. Not "I know they exist." Actually built in or integrated to them at depth.
You can journal a transaction without looking it up. You understand accrual versus cash basis, the close cycle, what a 1099 is for, and why a controller cares about the audit trail.
You have built either inside an accounting platform, on top of one as an integration partner, or built a fintech product that lives natively in the accounting workflow.
You understand the accountant channel and how CPAs influence product adoption. Bonus if you have built for or partnered with CPAs directly.
Typically 4 to 10 years of experience. Title is not the point.

Additional Information
We want to hear from you. We value passion, determination, and honesty. If you do not match every line of the spec but you can show us the work, apply anyway. Unusual paths and rare skills are how you stand out at Flex.

Deine Rolle
Als (Technical) Product Owner (m/w/d) bist du Teil unseres Product Teams und übernimmst Verantwortung für zentrale technische Schnittstellen und Integrationen unserer Plattformen. Dein Fokus liegt insbesondere auf unseren Customer APIs, der Unified Carrier Interface (UCI) sowie perspektivisch der Unified Financial Platform (UFP) und unserer HubSpot-Integration.
Dabei bewegst du dich an der Schnittstelle zwischen Product, Engineering und Business. Du verstehst technische Zusammenhänge, übersetzt unterschiedliche Anforderungen in klare Prioritäten und sorgst gemeinsam mit unseren Teams dafür, dass unsere Integrationen zuverlässig funktionieren und sich kontinuierlich weiterentwickeln.
Du arbeitest eng mit unseren Product Ownern, unserem Technical Business Analyst, Software Engineers und Data Insights zusammen und bist gleichzeitig wichtige Ansprechperson für interne Stakeholder, Kunden, Carrier und externe Partner.
Deine Aufgaben
Du übernimmst die Verantwortung für die Roadmap unserer Customer APIs für LMS Enterprise und LMS Next und entwickelst diese strategisch weiter.
Du treibst die Migration unserer API-Kunden von LMS Enterprise zu LMS Next voran und identifizierst, welche Features und Carrier-Integrationen dafür benötigt werden.
Du bist technische Ansprechperson für unsere API-Kunden und unterstützt bei Fragen sowie bei der Analyse und Lösung von Problemen.
Du verantwortest gemeinsam mit internen und externen Stakeholdern die Weiterentwicklung unserer Unified Carrier Interface (UCI).
Du analysierst Anforderungen an Carrier-Features und Services, bereitest diese für unser Engineering auf und unterstützt QA bei der Definition relevanter Test Cases.
Du stehst im direkten Austausch mit unseren Carriern und klärst technische Anforderungen und Besonderheiten rund um deren Integrationen.
Nach dem Go-live übernimmst du die Verantwortung für unsere Unified Financial Platform (UFP) und steuerst deren Backlog und Weiterentwicklung.
Du behältst unsere bestehende HubSpot-Integration im Blick und priorisierst Anpassungen entsprechend neuer Business-Anforderungen und Feedbacks.
Über alle Themen hinweg bringst du Engineering, Business Stakeholder, Carrier und externe Partner zusammen und sorgst für klare Anforderungen, Prioritäten und Entscheidungen.
Das bringst du mit
Du verfügst über einen technischen Hintergrund, beispielsweise in Software Engineering oder Informatik, oder hast bereits mehrere Jahre an der Schnittstelle zwischen Product und Engineering gearbeitet.
Du bringst Erfahrung als Product Owner oder Product Manager mit – idealerweise im Umfeld von APIs, Plattformen oder technischen Integrationen.
Du hast ein gutes Verständnis von APIs, API Design, Versionierung und Migrationsstrategien und kannst technische Diskussionen mit unseren Engineers auf Augenhöhe führen.
Du kannst komplexe technische Zusammenhänge verstehen und sie für unterschiedliche Stakeholder verständlich übersetzen.
Du bist sicher im Stakeholder Management und kannst unterschiedliche technische und wirtschaftliche Anforderungen gegeneinander abwägen und priorisieren.
Mehrere parallele Workstreams und wechselnde Prioritäten bringen dich nicht aus dem Konzept – du behältst den Überblick und setzt klare Schwerpunkte.
Du arbeitest gerne kollaborativ und standortübergreifend mit Kollegen in Hamburg und Naarden zusammen.
Du interessierst dich für AI Tools und digitale Lösungen und probierst gerne neue Wege aus, um Prozesse und Workflows effizienter zu gestalten.
Erfahrung in Logistik, Parcel oder Freight Tech, insbesondere mit Carrier-API-Integrationen, ist ein Plus.
Kenntnisse rund um HubSpot bzw. CRM-Integrationen oder Finanz- und Invoicing Systeme sind ebenfalls von Vorteil.

Bei uns erwartet dich ein Arbeitsumfeld, in dem neue Ideen ausdrücklich willkommen sind und Feedback nicht nur erlaubt, sondern erwünscht ist. The ideal candidate is an entrepreneurial builder who is energized by a blank canvas and knows how to take a big, ambiguous bet from zero to one.

You've worked in or close to telematics, connected vehicles, or connected devices, and you're equally comfortable going deep with engineering on how data flows in, negotiating a hardware or data partnership, and figuring out which customer experiences are worth building.

You have strong, loosely held opinions, make data-informed decisions, and care as much about reliability and data quality as velocity, because what you build is meant to become mission-critical to how fleets operate. Deepen and grow Fleetio's ecosystem of integrations and strategic partners from the tools fleets already use to OEM and telematics data providers.
Own how this data is standardized so it's trustworthy, comparable, and actionable everywhere it shows up across Fleetio.
Build and own strategic partner relationships, and serve as a credible product leader in front of partners.
Turn complex, real-world data flowing in from partners and connected sources into trustworthy, standardized, and actionable intelligence across Fleetio.
Partner with Design to make connected and partner-driven experiences intuitive, coherent, and genuinely useful.

We help organizations move from AI experimentation to measurable return on investment across four practices: AI Strategy and Advisory, Workforce Training and Enablement, Process Optimization, and Custom AI Development. Our work sits with executives and the people who do the work, and it is judged on whether something changed in production, not on whether a pilot looked good in a deck.

Ajaia is hiring a remote Product Manager to own products in Ajaia's product suite end to end. You will talk to users and customers every week, decide what gets built next and why, and say plainly what does not get built, including when the loudest voice in the room wants it.

You will write specs an engineer can build from without a follow-up meeting, prototype with AI tools when a working demo settles an argument faster than a deck, and stay on the number after launch and act on what it tells you. This is a builder's seat: you will contribute to the code and the design yourself, not only direct them.
You will work with a US-based team and US clients. Most of your users, stakeholders, and engineers sit in New York, so this role is built around daily overlap with US Eastern hours, not asynchronous handoffs.
Compensation: Competitive, benchmarked to senior product roles in your market, plus a performance bonus tied to product outcomes. We will share a specific number for your location early in the process.
How we expect you to work
AI use is a core execution requirement at Ajaia, not optional tooling. You will use AI daily to sort through usage data, draft specs, and build working prototypes yourself, and you are judged on what you keep from that output, not on how much of it you generated. The tools change fast, and staying current on what is worth using is part of the job.
Remote works here when the writing is strong. Decisions, specs, and priority calls get written down where the team can read them, not held in your head until the next call.

Talk to users and customers every week. Not a quarterly survey. Real conversations, real usage, on US time.
Turn messy, sometimes contradictory signal, usage data, support tickets, sales requests, and what people say in interviews, into a ranked call on what gets built next.
Say plainly what does not get built, including a well-funded customer's request, when the evidence does not support it.
Write specs an engineer can build from without a follow-up meeting: the outcome, what is in and out of scope, where a human stays in the loop, and acceptance criteria someone could test.
Prototype the core flow yourself, wireframes, a clickable mock, or a working demo, when that settles the argument faster than a deck would.
Contribute to the code and the design directly: ship a small feature or fix with AI tools, mock the screen yourself, and hand engineers something running instead of something described.
Partner with the design team on what the solution should be and how it holds up for the people using it.
Partner with the delivery team and engineers on how the build runs and the date it ships by.
Present the roadmap and the tradeoffs to the people who fund it, including when a client or a salesperson is unhappy with the call.
Hold a priority decision under real pushback, or change it, and say why either way.
Ship it, then watch the number after launch and act on what it says.

At Google, we put our users first. The world is always changing, so we need Product Managers who are continuously adapting and excited to work on products that affect millions of people every day.
In this role, you will work cross-functionally to guide products from conception to launch by connecting the technical and business worlds. You can break down complex problems into steps that drive product development.
One of the many reasons Google consistently brings innovative, world-changing products to market is because of the collaborative work we do in Product Management. In the AI era, users expect Search to effortlessly Answer, Explore, and Address Anything. To meet these rising expectations, our models need the content.
The Search Content Platform (SCP) team builds an AI-first content platform to deliver a comprehensive and trustworthy knowledge source. By acquiring third-party data and organizing disparate modalities-such as text, images, videos, and User-Generated Content-into a seamless whole, we make Search AI experiences rich, helpful, and performant.
Our team's mission is to use AI to revolutionize how we acquire and organize third-party content. As the Group Product Manager for Content Acquisition and Identity, you will manage a team to define the future of Google Search content. You will collaborate with engineering teams in Zurich, Sao Paulo, and Mountain View, and represent the organization to key partners.
In Google Search, we're reimagining what it means to search for information - any way and anywhere. To do that, we need to solve complex engineering challenges and expand our infrastructure, while maintaining a universally accessible and useful experience that people around the world rely on. In joining the Search team, you'll have an opportunity to make an impact on billions of people globally.

* Lead the product goal, detailed platform requirements for a horizontal content acquisition platform that accelerates third-party (3P) content acquisition while delivering on critical priority verticals such as Sports and Health.
* Enable Search to answer billions of user queries daily by innovating on content identity for the AI era and establishing clear, disambiguated, and precise identities for billions of user queries on Search daily.
* Direct efforts to analyze billions of current and aspirational user queries that lack sufficient content, and prioritize or drive initiatives to bridge these gaps and improve product helpfulness to end users.
* Discuss your knowledge and use of AI tools during the hiring process to demonstrate the AI fluency expected in this role.

This role starts on the content platform, and the platform surface it serves is growing. The foundations of the company, identity and access, developer platform, data and the infrastructure everything runs on, are being invested in over the coming year. We are looking for someone whose curiosity does not stop at the edge of their own team, because the interesting problems here sit exactly where those layers meet.
There is genuine ambiguity in this space right now, and a decision or two you would inherit that we have not finished making. We would rather tell you that than have you discover it in month two. The upside is that very little here is set, so the person who takes this shapes the layer everything else in the product is built on for the next several years.

Own the content services every surface depends on. The services and APIs that serve content to the learner surface, the admin surface and everything we build next, plus the delivery path including CDN and video, and file and asset storage.
Own the structural contract. How content is stored, versioned and served so it can be reused and assembled differently for different customers. This is a schema and interface problem before it is a tooling problem, and your measure is whether the contract other teams build against is clear, stable and safe to change.
Own multi tenant separation. Making sure one customer’s content and branding stay theirs. The tenancy model needs a decision and an owner, and that will be one of your first real pieces of work.
Own access, entitlements and data residency. Who can reach what, where data lives, and what we are able to commit to contractually.
Own performance and cost per tenant. If this layer is slow, everything is slow. If it is expensive, it is expensive everywhere.
Carry the platform half of a migration already in flight. We are moving off an incumbent content tool while the current system keeps earning. Sequencing that is the real work, and the order matters more than the ambition.
Own the non functional questions that show up in deals. A meaningful share of our deals slow down in security and compliance review rather than in the pitch, and that is a product problem with a revenue number attached.

s.h: This role is for you if you have
s.t:
Experience with content management as a product, whether that is a CMS, a DAM, a headless content platform or a structured content system at scale. This is our primary preference.
Experience owning platform or infrastructure adjacent product, where success was measured in what other teams could build rather than in features a customer names.
Enough technical depth to be useful and the honesty to say where you are not. You can read an architecture proposal, ask the question that unpicks it, and tell the difference between a researched answer and a fluent one.
The ability to hold your own with senior engineers, infrastructure engineers and security specialists. Not as a peer on implementation, but well enough that a remediation estimate or a tenancy design does not go unchallenged. A previous career as an engineer is a real advantage and not a requirement.
A habit of thinking in seams. Where systems meet, what a contract between them should guarantee, and how to keep a decision reversible rather than walking through a one way door.
The ability to sequence. We are modernising a platform that carries real history while it keeps earning, and the order matters more than the ambition.
Writing. Decisions, tradeoffs and the reasoning behind them, in a way an engineer and an executive can both act on.
Nice to have, and genuinely useful: depth in AI and personalisation, or in infrastructure. Either one compounds with this role, and we are not expecting both.

s.h: This role is not for you if
s.t:
You want to be a delivery manager for the engineers. They are strong and they do not need coordinating. They need decisions and clarity about what matters.
You want to own the authoring and editorial experience itself. A colleague owns that, you will work closely with them, and drawing the seam between you well is part of the job.
You want to run a rewrite programme. Foundations serve outcomes, and a foundation with no customer outcome attached does not get funded here and should not.
You need the surrounding decisions settled before you arrive.

Not the language apps, which have the habit but not the stakes. Not the platforms, which have the content but not the attention. As our Senior Product Manager for the learner experience, you own the surface where learning actually happens, for the person actually doing it. It is the most visible product role in the company, because everything else in our strategy depends on somebody coming back on a Tuesday. Today weekly active learners sits close to one percent. That number is the job.

Own the learner surface end to end. Onboarding, what someone is offered next, how it arrives, and what we learn from what they did.
Move us from a catalogue people browse to a product that pays attention. Personalisation here is a spectrum, not a feature: country and industry, company size, whether they reach us through their own LMS or directly, then company, department, team and finally the individual. A fifteen minute bus ride should be able to become seven minutes of audio and three quick questions, assembled for that person.
Partner with our educational designers on how it reaches one person. They have decades of research behind how our content is built, in activities of two to eight minutes designed for habit formation. What is not yet settled is how those pieces compose into a path for one person, and you would be one of the people settling it.

Your half is the one they cannot do on their own: how it reaches one specific person, on one specific day, on whatever device they have, and what to offer instead when something did not land.
Own the measurement that makes it real. Weekly active learners is the number this role moves. There is a baseline. Setting the target with us, and owning the path to it, is part of the job.
Treat mobile as a first class question rather than a port. Seven minutes attached to a real week is a phone experience far more often than a desk one. Whether that is a native client or something lighter is a genuine open decision with very different costs.
Draw on a single library. Our own studio content, customer created content and content generated on the spot all sit together, and deciding what surfaces to whom is part of your job.
This role is for you if you have
A track record owning either a B2B2C product, where the buyer and the user are different people and the user did not choose you, or a consumer habit-formation product built to create usage rather than meet demand that already existed
Evidence you have shipped personalisation, routing or recommendation work that measurably changed behaviour, and the scar tissue to know how often it does not
Comfort on a platform that carries real history. You will build the new thing while the old thing earns the revenue, and sequencing that is part of the craft rather than an obstacle to it
A habit of deciding. You gather input properly and then take the call, and you can say clearly what you are not doing and why
A habit of working in the open. Drafts early, thinking visible, and you would rather be corrected on Tuesday than right on Friday
A genuine interest in how people learn. You do not need a background in it, you do need to find it interesting, because you will work closely with people who have spent careers on it
Comfort partnering with an embedded engineering manager on the team rather than managing engineers directly
This role is not for you if
You want a clean greenfield. That is a much easier engineering problem and a much worse bet, and it is not what this is
You need the strategy finished before you start. It is being written now and you would be one of the people writing it
You want to run the roadmap process. Product Operations owns that craft, this role owns the outcome
You would rather own a feature area than a number

Constructor powers product search and discovery for some of the largest retailers in the world. We serve billions of requests every week, and you’ve probably seen our results somewhere and used our product without knowing it.

We differentiate ourselves by focusing on metrics over features, and reinventing search and discovery from the ground up as a machine learning challenge with the specific goal of improving metrics like revenue. We’re approximately doubling year over year despite the market slowing down and have customers in every eCommerce vertical.

We’re a passionate team of technologists who love solving problems and want to make our customers’ and coworkers’ lives better. We value empathy, openness, curiosity, continuous improvement, and are excited by metrics that matter. We believe that empowering everyone in a company to do what they think is best can lead to great things.

We’re looking for a highly technical, systems-minded Senior Product Manager to lead two critical search intelligence teams: Machine Learning & Recall and Query . Search at Constructor is fundamentally an ML challenge, and this role sits at the absolute entry point of our discovery pipeline, right where shopper intent meets candidate retrieval.
In this role, you will bridge the Query team (understanding what a shopper means across intent, entities, and language) with the Machine Learning & Recall team (retrieving the exact right set of candidate products across massive catalogs).

You will define strategy across both domains, balancing state-of-the-art techniques, such as vector search, semantic parsing, dense embeddings, and LLM-assisted query interpretation, with low-latency production execution.

You won’t be measured on shipping features for the sake of it; you’ll be measured on candidate quality, query accuracy, and driving business outcomes like conversion rate, search-attributed revenue, and revenue per visit.

Set a unified roadmap: Define the multi-quarter vision and strategy across both the Machine Learning & Recall and Query teams, ensuring query understanding and candidate generation evolve hand-in-hand.
Drive Query intelligence: Lead the Query team to push boundaries in tokenization, spell correction, entity extraction, intent classification, and LLM-assisted query parsing across multiple languages.
Advance Recall systems: Lead the Machine Learning & Recall team in evolving candidate generation architecture, seamlessly combining traditional keyword search with modern dense embeddings, vector retrieval, and hybrid recall models.
Move core business metrics: Own measurable lift in search-attributed conversion, revenue per visit, and GMV across all retail customer verticals.
Turn research into production wins: Work shoulder-to-shoulder with ML researchers, data scientists, and software engineers to take SOTA models from research to low-latency, cost-effective production systems.
Balance ML performance trade-offs: Make data-backed decisions balancing model complexity, accuracy, inference latency, compute costs, and real-time execution constraints.
Build evaluation frameworks: Establish robust offline and online measurement systems to evaluate retrieval precision and query understanding accuracy against customer revenue outcomes.
Orchestrate pipeline handoffs: Ensure candidate product sets and query context flow cleanly into downstream ranking and search quality models without signal loss.
Solve systemic issues: Lead technical triage when query interpretation or retrieval anomalies occur, building durable, automated fixes rather than one-off patches.
What Success Looks Like

Driven quantifiable lift in search-attributed conversion and revenue per visit across major customer verticals.
Stood up an integrated evaluation framework connecting query parsing and candidate recall directly to business outcomes.
Optimized inference latency and compute infrastructure to ensure high-capacity ML models run fast and cost-effectively in production.
